title: notes to self — quick daily scratchpad
content:
Daily scratchpad — quick brain dump (Mar 4)

Morning plan:
- 9:00 stand-up: update on KV cache flakiness (show recent logs)
- Finish SUMMARY of benchmark runs for 2-token batching change (INF-3421) — need numbers for p95 latency and token cost delta
- PR review: #1284 (fallback routing) — leave comment about metrics to emit (route_reason, fallback_from)

Immediate TODOs:
- Reproduce cache eviction case on devbox: run job with seq_len=1024, batch_size variations (1,4,8) — capture timeline of cache hits
- Add small unit test for policy selection edge-case (when model variant mismatch) — quick mock ok
- Ping Alex about dedicated pool rollout schedule + DB migration window (we need a 1-hour quiet window)
- Reply to Jordan re: canary config for canary group sizes (he suggested 2% — check math vs load)

Notes / observations:
- Benchmark notes: 2-token batching reduces avg cost per token ~6% on A100 but increases p95 by ~18ms in worst cases (likely due to batching wait time). Need to try adaptive batching threshold.
- Saw repeated 429s from region-eu-2 at 03/03 22:14 UTC — correlates with autoscaler thrash? Check cloud logs and autoscaler events.
- Local repro failed because my dataset had much shorter average prompt length — toss in some long prompts from privacy-safe eval set.

Questions to resolve:
- If we enable adaptive batching, what should be the fallback when p95 exceeds SLO? immediate disable? gradual degrade?
- How aggressive can cache TTL be for private deployments without breaking privacy/KMS assumptions? (ask security)

Short personal reminders (one-off):
- Pick up passport copy from Post Office before 5pm (deadline Fri)
- Groceries: milk, eggs, baby spinach, tofu (quick list)
- Call dentist to reschedule (number in phone)

Meeting prep for 1:30pm w/ product-hosted-api:
- Bring 2 slides: "batching vs latency tradeoffs" and "fallback routing options and metrics"
- Ask PM for customer examples where p95 matters > avg cost savings

Scratch ideas (brainstorm, not polished):
- small agent that monitors p95 drift and automatically adjusts batching threshold per-route (fast feedback loop)
- lightweight synthetic traffic generator that mimics 95th percentile prompt distributions for continuous regressions

Random notes to self:
- Save current run logs to S3 under /debug/runs/2026-03-04/samira/ before cleaning workspace
- TODO: consolidate my scattered notes into a proper ticket with steps to reproduce + minimal repro dataset

Done-for-now list (feel-good):
- pushed WIP PR for fallback routing instrumentation
- slid bench numbers into deck draft (needs cleanup)

-- SAMIRA
